summary: Initial discovery with Caspian Analytics evaluating migration from OpenAI to Redwood Dedicated. Main drivers: cost predictability, latency consistency, and data residency. Discussed eval parity, compatibility with vLLM/TGI, pilot benchmark, and security requirements. Agreed to run a short perf pilot and share security docs and pricing.
transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-04
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Avery Chen (Redwood AE), Riley Park (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (CTO - Caspian), Liam O'Connor (Lead ML Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Security), Ben Park (PM)
---
[00:00] Avery Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Avery from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. we also have Riley our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:06] Maya Singh: Good, thanks. Sorry, quick note we got hit by Bud schedule crunch so we've got about 45 minutes.
[00:10] Avery Chen: Perfect, we'll keep it tight. goal today: understand your current stack, pain points, and what success looks like for moving off OpenAI to something like Redwood Dedicated or Private.
[00:18] Ben Park: Yep, high level from our side: we run a large set of customer-facing assistants and internal summarization pipelines on OpenAI today. cost has spiked and variability in latency is causing UI flakiness.
[00:28] Liam O'Connor: Also want to validate model/eval parity — the outputs have to be indistinguishably close to our current setup. We use some custom few-shot prompts and a post-rank step.
[00:36] Riley Park: Got it. so two threads: infra/ops (cost, latency, reliability) and output parity / compatibility. quick Q: are you running any local inference libs like vLLM or TGI right now, or strictly OpenAI?
[00:46] Liam O'Connor: Mostly strictly OpenAI API. We have a small research cluster running vLLM for experiments but nothing in production.
[00:52] Sofia Ruiz: From security: we need SOC2, KMS integration for keys, SSO (SAML), audit logs, and some customers require data residency in EU.
[01:02] Avery Chen: All very common asks. Redwood Dedicated supports VPC/network isolation, KMS/HSM integrations, and we provide SOC2 reports; I'll share the whitepaper. we can also support private control plane for the strict customers.
[01:12] Maya Singh: Quick on pricing: is Dedicated a straight per-token or committed capacity plus overage?
[01:18] Avery Chen: Typically reserved capacity with monthly/annual commits. you get predictable throughput and lower unit costs, and then burst options. I'll send the tiers after the call.
[01:26] Ben Park: About compatibility — our team wrote an adapter to the OpenAI API. we need to know how much code change to expect. does Redwood expose OpenAI-compatible endpoints?
[01:34] Riley Park: Redwood API is intentionally similar: REST/SDKs for text, chat, embeddings. in many cases it's a drop-in with minor path changes. where there are differences we provide some compatibility shim and an SDK. also we can host models that match the ones you currently call.
[01:44] Liam O'Connor: Ok. we also use the OpenAI streaming chunks and rely on token-level latencies. how does Redwood handle streaming, and will latency improve on Dedicated?
[01:54] Riley Park: We support streaming responses; on Dedicated you get predictable tail latency because of reserved GPUs and tuned batching. that said it's dependent on model size and sequence lengths — we can run benchmarks using your eval set.
[02:06] Maya Singh: You mentioned kernel selection and optimizations in the literature — we run both short prompt chat and long-context summarization, so mixed seq length workload. any gotchas with KV cache across requests?
[02:18] Riley Park: We manage KV cache per session and have smart caching for prefixes — can be turned on/off. for long-context summarization we tune chunking and offload. again bench is the best way to surface that.
[02:30] Sofia Ruiz: On the security side, do you support customer-managed KMS? and is data encrypted at rest and in transit?
[02:38] Avery Chen: Yes, customer-managed KMS is supported for Private and Dedicated (depending on the plan). encryption in transit and rest yes, plus audit logs and RBAC. we'll send the SOC2 and an architecture diagram.
[02:48] Ben Park: Great. on eval parity: we care about not just lexical similarity but regression on our quality metrics. can we run the same prompts and get token-level outputs to compare?
[02:56] Riley Park: Absolutely. we can run a perf and quality benchmark. typical approach: 1) we ingest your eval set, 2) run scaled queries on Dedicated, 3) compare metrics (perplexity/ROUGE/LLM-specific scores) and sample diffs.
[03:10] Liam O'Connor: How about the runtime underneath — if we want to run vLLM/TGI on our infra later, will models exported from Redwood be compatible?
[03:20] Riley Park: Redwood's runtime is model-format agnostic for many common model formats. we support common HF formats and some quantization profiles. that said, if you plan to self-host with vLLM/TGI there may be differences in kernel-level performance; we'll help identify quantization + conversion steps.
[03:34] Maya Singh: Any customers who've migrated from OpenAI and kept parity? examples?
[03:38] Avery Chen: Yes, a/b customers in fintech and e-commerce ran pilots — we have case notes. one note: small prompt tuning and few-shot examples sometimes need slight rework around tokenization/stop sequences. but overall parity was achievable.
[03:50] Ben Park: That rework is doable. timeline: we want to have a pilot in Q2, slides to exec by end of the month.
[03:58] Avery Chen: Sounds reasonable. Proposed pilot: 1-week Dedicated sandbox with your eval set, run traffic that approximates production, and collect perf + quality metrics.
[04:08] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot infra, what do we need to set up? network peering? VPN?
[04:14] Riley Park: For Dedicated sandbox we typically need VPC peering or a secure peering method, service account credentials, and sample traffic. we have an infra checklist. I'll include it in the follow-up.
[04:24] Sofia Ruiz: Data residency — we have EU customers. can you guarantee EU region hosting and separate logs?
[04:30] Avery Chen: Yes we have region controls and can set data locality by deployment. logs can be isolated per tenant in Dedicated.
[04:36] Ben Park: A few technical questions from Liam: 1) Do you expose token-level logs for debugging? 2) How do you handle model fallbacks if a node is full?
[04:46] Riley Park: 1) Token-level traces can be provided with redaction controls. 2) We have smart routing and fallback to compatible model variants; for Dedicated you can configure fallback policies (e.g., lower-cost model or degrade gracefully).
[04:58] Liam O'Connor: About cost: do we get clearer unit economics compared to OpenAI? we want predictable SW budgets.
[05:06] Avery Chen: Yes, reserved capacity gives a predictable price per token equivalent and we provide tooling (Redwood Optimize) for batching/caching recommendations to lower unit cost.
[05:14] Maya Singh: Any blockers for us to start the benchmark? we need a non-prod account and access for us to upload evals.
[05:22] Avery Chen: We'll provision a sandbox Dedicated instance for the pilot; you'll get temporary credentials and an upload endpoint. Riley will send the exact steps.
[05:28] Ben Park: We might also run a side-by-side test against vLLM on our research cluster to see differences. is that supported?
[05:34] Riley Park: Yes, we can export logs and model artifacts to enable comparison. sometimes floating-point/quant differences show up but we can annotate.
[05:42] Sofia Ruiz: On compliance: will Redwood sign a DPA with our standard flow?
[05:46] Avery Chen: We have DPA templates and have signed with similar customers. our legal team can iterate if you have custom clauses.
[05:52] Maya Singh: Ok, let's talk risk: if we roll out and see regressions in quality, what's the rollback story?
[05:58] Riley Park: We recommend canary rollouts with traffic split and automatic fallback to the original provider if regressions exceed thresholds. Redwood supports A/B and automatic rollback policies.
[06:08] Liam O'Connor: Good to know. small nit: some of your docs call it Redwood Dedicate — I think a typo popped in earlier.
[06:14] Avery Chen: ah yes, that's our bad — we'll fix doc typos.
[06:18] Ben Park: Any constraints on model sizes? we use a mix: small chat models for UI and a few 30B-ish models for long context.
[06:26] Riley Park: Dedicated supports a range of model sizes; performance profiles vary. for the large LMs we recommend specific GPU types and quantization profiles. we'll include recommended configs in the benchmark deck.
[06:36] Maya Singh: For the benchmark, can we get token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99)?
[06:40] Riley Park: Yes, Redwood Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route. we'll surface p50/p95/p99.
[06:46] Sofia Ruiz: Audit logs format? we need syslog/export to our SIEM.
[06:52] Avery Chen: We can stream audit logs to your SIEM or provide secure dump exports; we'll include integration guides.
[06:58] Ben Park: Any notes on running the post-ranker step — we do reranking and then re-score. can Redwood host a reranker or should we run it in our infra?
[07:06] Riley Park: You can do either. many teams keep rerankers in their infra for control, but we support function-calling style hooks; we can host rerankers inside Dedicated if preferred.
[07:14] Maya Singh: Sounds flexible. ok we need to lock down next steps and owners.
[07:18] Avery Chen: Recap and next steps: 1) Avery send pricing and tiers + SOC2/security deck. 2) Riley send pilot infra checklist and benchmark instructions. 3) Liam share eval set and sample traffic shape. 4) Schedule kickoff for the week of Mar 16. Anyone want different items?
[07:34] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. I'll share eval set by Friday.
[07:38] Sofia Ruiz: I'll compile security Qs and send them to Avery.
[07:40] Ben Park: I'll coordinate exec slide draft.
[07:44] Avery Chen: Great — timeline wise, we'll aim to have the sandbox provisioned within 7 business days once evals are received.
[07:52] Maya Singh: One last quick Q: vendor lock-in concerns — if we ever move off Redwood, what's data migration like?
[07:58] Riley Park: We provide export tools and model artifacts for supported formats; we try to minimize lock-in and document conversion steps for vLLM/TGI.
[08:08] Maya Singh: Perfect. thanks everyone.
[08:10] Avery Chen: Thanks all, we'll follow up with the deck and checklist. Appreciate the time.
---
End of call.
Notes: Transcription includes occasional mis-hears (e.g., Redwood Dedicate). Some technical terms may be slightly garbled (v LLM / TGI).
